target_customer: US millennials and consumers wanting a simple chat based personal finance coach
problem: Budgeting apps like Mint are complex; Penny used a chat interface to tell users their spending, bills and forecasts.
business_model: Free consumer app planned to monetize later via machine learning products and partnerships

founders.name: Mitch Lee
founders.background_notes: YC page bio. TechCrunch calls him Mitchell Lee, co-founder. No education or earlier employers in opened sources.

founders.name: Alex Quach
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; no background.

competitors.name: Mint
competitors.traction_then: VentureBeat headline framed Penny as taking on Mint; user numbers not opened

technical_complexity.rationale: Bank data aggregation and a conversational interface with forecasts were standard but non trivial work for two founders.

defensibility.rationale: Chat finance coaching was copyable and aggregation APIs were commodity.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Credit Karma acquired Penny in March 2018 and used its conversational tech; the Penny app was shut down.

market_need_then: Chat bots were fashionable in 2016 and budgeting apps were popular; the app served hundreds of thousands of people per Credit Karma.

branding.name_origin: A Product Hunt founder comment says the name plays on the one cent coin and works as a catchy personal name, also a woman's name.

identity.mascot_or_character: Penny, a chat persona who greets users
identity.visual_style: Chat interface with graphs and emojis per Springwise

branding.brand_signature: A named chat persona for money advice

brand_strength.rationale: A personified brand with press coverage by TechCrunch and VentureBeat, but several other apps share the name.

outcome_analysis: Penny launched as a chat based finance coach in 2015, raised a 1.2 million dollar seed from Social Capital in May 2016 and joined YC in Winter 2017. Credit Karma acquired it in March 2018 for undisclosed terms, shut the standalone app and used the team and technology for conversational features, which looks like a soft landing for a small consumer app.
notes: pennyapp.io is now a farewell page saying Penny was acquired by Credit Karma. Credit Karma's post says March without a year; other sources say 2018 and the post implies it. A 120K YC pre seed in 2017 appears only on an aggregator and is not recorded. CB Insights total of 1.32 million is unverified. A UK pension app called Penny is unrelated. Competitor list is thin: TechCrunch named none; only the VentureBeat headline was seen. Whether the team joined Credit Karma is not stated. Failure factor is inference.
